reuse.why: The tolerance comes from the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts, and the rule is added to the existing getScheduledAmount that every planning site already calls.

duplication.why: The 7.5% tolerance and the worst-case rule are each defined once, and callers only pass their operator.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside the ranged worst-case rule and reuses the matching tolerance from shared/rules.

scope.why: The edits are many but nearly all are the necessary one-argument call-site updates. The forecast normaliser gains its own operator-resolution expression.

maintainability.why: The single definition is clean, but adding amountOp as a positional parameter before the existing `inverse` flag silently changes the meaning of any positional call, and the operator is typed as a loose string.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every planning caller routes through getScheduledAmount, and the edit-form conversions in useScheduleEdit stay operator-agnostic as before.

one_place.where: getScheduledAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts, now taking the operator, used by every planning path: API, template, forecast, preview, posting and the UI totals.
